title: Visual Novel Art with Krita and Stable Diffusion (Game demo released!)
author: SnooWalruses5620
selftext:
Hi guys, maybe some people have seen my earlier post. This post doubles as a guide and self promo. **I recently released a DEMO of my game at** [https://coffeemist.itch.io/otome-or-not](https://coffeemist.itch.io/otome-or-not) ! A meta mystery visual novel disguised as an otome.   
*Shameless self promo!*

  
Now onto the guide...  
This is a quick workflow video of the process I've been using to create the art for my visual novel both CGs and sprites included. I found that there are very few videos around for those wanting to have full control over a subject and background so this video is an attempt to give more insight.

Some details on my process:

* **3D TO 2D,** one of the hurdles I faced is I wanted very specific posing and angles, using a 3d image I was able to keep exact angle and character poses. This process done by using a 3D model base posed in MMD preprocessed into the 2d drawing.
* **NO LORAs used** character consistency is all done purely with control net and prompt (I just never felt like making Loras and now I'm too deep in my own rabbit hole...)
* **Local models only!** I use purely local models for SDXL on my computer to gen everything (I have no subscriptions at all for online ai services 🙃 )
* What about backgrounds? Backgrounds were done by taking 3d sketch up models, angling the camera on the exact perspective and then post processed with flux. I plan to do a background video at some point but haven't gotten around to recording one...

  
Now I'll shamelessly link a video my game's trailer [https://youtu.be/hT8VaOqtBoo?si=-SfXjKZFvxve6DWg](https://youtu.be/hT8VaOqtBoo?si=-SfXjKZFvxve6DWg) 😅 

Thanks for reading! I try to post process videos on my channel if you feel like keeping an eye out. If  my game is of interest to you feel free to check it out too!
